capabilities: sync notes, attachments, and optional .obsidian configuration across devices via a self-hosted server
resolve sync conflicts with revision-based CAS, keep-local/remote/both, and three-way Markdown merge
share individual notes and folders via links and publish a public blog from the server
collaborate on Markdown notes through invitations with SSE or long-polling delivery
manage vault files through a web console with previews, history, diffs, restore, and a recycle bin
extras: README warns that WASM server plugins are not guaranteed safe, that failed upgrades cannot reverse database migrations, and that /readyz is not a complete end-to-end sync health check; detailed deployment and development guides live outside the README.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to self-host multi-device sync, file sharing, and publishing on your own server.

requires.name: account on the configured OSS Sync server

summary: Self-hosted sync and share system with a single-binary Go server for multi-device note sync, conflict resolution, sharing links, blogs, and Markdown collaboration.
